metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Occupational Health and Safety Platform domain: the lifecycle Know the workforce -> Plan surveillance -> Examine and advise -> Keep the medical file -> Assess and control risks -> Handle events -> Serve employees and managers -> Prove compliance as run by internal occupational health services, HSE and prevention teams, HR administrators, managers and employees of large organisations in France, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands on Kitry, plus the deployment, migration, training and integration journeys run by Kitry's own consultants.
metadata.flowModelNote: Each stream carries only stream-specific flows, names the supporting bricks used in each step and the persona acting in it (occupational physician, nurse, service manager, HSE manager, site manager, HR administrator, employee, Kitry consultant), and lists the external systems (HRIS, identity providers, Goodflag e-signature, Vonage teleconsultation, Cegedim SMS, connected measurement devices, national reporting portals such as net-entreprises/Ameli and Fedris, work accident insurers, HDS/ISO 27001 hosting) the flow depends on.

rootGroups.name: Occupational Health Streams
rootGroups.description: From HRIS feeds and workstation exposures to examined workers with signed fitness opinions and a complete confidential medical file: the journeys that keep the workforce and exposure data current, plan and schedule surveillance, run examinations and teleconsultations, and keep the occupational medical file.

streams.name: Maintain workforce and exposure data
streams.description: Keep a current register of every worker, contract, assignment, site and workstation from HRIS feeds and the customer's organisational structure, and attach to each workstation the exposure and risk profile (night work, chemical, biological and physical agents, safety-critical posts, Belgian 'postes de vigilance' and 'postes à risque défini') that determines which surveillance category applies. This is the connected record on which convocations, fitness opinions, the risk assessment, event declarations and every annual report rely: when HR moves a worker to a new post, the platform knows the new exposures and the surveillance it triggers.
outcomes: Every active worker has a current assignment, workstation and exposure profile, so surveillance is derived rather than decided by hand
HRIS changes (hire, transfer, contract end, long absence) reach the medical service within a day and trigger the right visit automatically
Workstation exposure profiles are shared by the physician and the prevention adviser, so the medical and the safety view of a post never diverge
Data quality exceptions (workers without a workstation, workstations without an exposure profile, duplicates) are visible and worked down

flows.title: Synchronise the Workforce from the HRIS
flows.description: The HR administrator lets the nightly HRIS feed create, update and close worker, contract and assignment records; the service coordinator reviews exceptions, maps new organisational units and workstations and confirms that each worker sits on a workstation with an exposure profile.
flows.trigger: A nightly or weekly HRIS export arrives, or HR records a hire, transfer, contract end or long absence.
flows.successSignal: The import batch is applied without unresolved exceptions, every active worker has a workstation and exposure profile, and surveillance recalculates for the changed workers.

steps.title: Receive and validate the HRIS batch
keyFacts: The batch carries employee identifiers, civil status, contract type and dates, organisational unit, cost centre, job title, site and absence periods; the platform validates format, referential integrity and duplicates before applying anything.
Multi-entity customers such as a group with French and Belgian subsidiaries run one feed per legal entity so that country-specific rules apply to the right population.
painPoints: HR exports that rename organisational units silently detach hundreds of workers from their workstation.
Rejected rows that nobody reads mean a new hire never receives the visite d'information et de prévention within the three months the French Labour Code requires.

dependencies.name: HRIS Synchronisation and Import
dependencies.how: Receives the export, validates rows and reports rejects per batch.

dependencies.name: Worker, Contract and Assignment Registry
dependencies.how: Applies creates, updates and closures to the worker registry.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail and Data Retention
dependencies.how: Records who imported what and which records changed.

steps.title: Map new organisational units, sites and workstations
keyFacts: New HR units are mapped to sites and workstations in the platform's own structure, which can be finer than HR (a 'production operator' in HR can be three workstations with different exposures).
Belgian customers align sites with the scope of the internal prevention service and the CPPT; French customers align with the SPST sector and the établissement for the DUERP.
painPoints: HR structures follow payroll and reporting lines, not exposures, so a naive one-to-one mapping loses the information the physician needs.
Sites created ad hoc by different administrators lead to duplicate workstations and split surveillance history.

dependencies.name: Organisation, Sites and Workstations
dependencies.how: Maintains the mapping between HR units and platform sites and workstations.

dependencies.name: Configuration Engine
dependencies.how: Holds customer-specific mapping rules and default workstations per job title.

steps.title: Assign workers to workstations and confirm exposures
keyFacts: Each assignment links the worker to a workstation and inherits its exposure profile; HR can add individual exposures (a worker who occasionally drives a forklift) without altering the workstation.
A change of workstation closes the previous assignment with an end date so that exposure history is preserved for the medical file and later occupational disease claims.
painPoints: Workers left on a generic 'to be assigned' workstation are invisible to surveillance planning.
Overwriting an assignment instead of closing it erases the exposure history that a Fedris or CPAM occupational disease file will require years later.

dependencies.name: Worker, Contract and Assignment Registry
dependencies.how: Creates and closes assignments with effective dates.

dependencies.name: Exposure and Risk Profile Register
dependencies.how: Derives the worker's exposure profile from the workstation plus individual additions.

steps.title: Work the data quality exception list
keyFacts: The exception list shows workers without workstation, workstations without exposure profile, duplicate persons, contracts ending without a closing visit and workers imported but never seen by the service.
Exceptions are assigned to HR or to the medical service and their age is tracked, because a stale exception is a missed visit.
painPoints: Service coordinators discover data gaps only when the annual report shows a coverage rate below target.
Duplicates created by a change of employee number split a worker's medical history across two records.

dependencies.name: Worker, Contract and Assignment Registry
dependencies.how: Lists and assigns worker and assignment exceptions.

dependencies.name: HRIS Synchronisation and Import
dependencies.how: Re-applies corrected rows from earlier batches.

steps.title: Recalculate surveillance for changed workers
keyFacts: For every changed assignment the periodicity engine re-derives the surveillance category and next due visit: a move to a night-shift post in France converts a five-yearly VIP into a three-yearly one; a Belgian worker moving to a safety function enters periodic health assessment.
The coordinator sees a summary of visits added, advanced or removed before the plan is updated.
painPoints: Recalculation done by hand in spreadsheets lags weeks behind HR reality.
Visits that disappear because a worker left are not cancelled in the physician's agenda, wasting scarce medical time.

dependencies.name: Surveillance Rules and Periodicity Engine
dependencies.how: Re-derives category and due dates for changed workers.

dependencies.name: Country Regulation Content
dependencies.how: Supplies FR/BE/LU/NL surveillance categories and intervals.

steps.title: Confirm the batch and notify the medical service
keyFacts: The applied batch is confirmed with counts of workers created, updated and closed and the resulting surveillance changes; the medical service receives a digest rather than raw HR data.
The audit trail keeps the batch, its source file and every field change for the retention period, which matters when a worker contests a missed visit.
painPoints: HR and the medical service work from different lists and argue about who is on the payroll.
Without a batch record it is impossible to explain to the labour inspector why a worker was not convened.

dependencies.name: HRIS Synchronisation and Import
dependencies.how: Closes the batch with counts and status.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail and Data Retention
dependencies.how: Retains batch and field-level history.

flows.title: Define Workstation Exposure Profiles with the Physician and the Prevention Adviser
flows.description: The prevention adviser and the physician review a site's workstations, record the exposures and risk factors of each, classify them into surveillance categories per country, and publish the profile so that assignments, the risk assessment and surveillance planning use the same source.
flows.trigger: A new site, line or job is created, a risk assessment reveals a new exposure, or the annual review of the workstation list is due.
flows.successSignal: Every workstation on the site has a published exposure profile with a surveillance category agreed by the physician, and the affected workers' surveillance is recalculated.

steps.title: List the workstations of the site
keyFacts: The prevention adviser lists workstations per site and line, reusing the structure that the DUERP or global prevention plan already uses, so a workstation is one object for safety and for health.

In Belgium the list also identifies safety functions and 'postes de vigilance', 'postes à risque défini' and 'activités à risque défini' under the Code on well-being at work, the categories that legally require health surveillance.
painPoints: Prevention services keep their own workstation list in a spreadsheet that never matches the medical service's list.
Job titles are used as a proxy for workstations, hiding that the same title covers very different exposures.

dependencies.name: Organisation, Sites and Workstations
dependencies.how: Maintains workstations per site and line.

dependencies.name: Risk Assessment and Prevention Plan
dependencies.how: Reuses the workstations already assessed in the risk assessment.

steps.title: Record exposures and risk factors per workstation
keyFacts: Exposures are picked from a controlled list: chemical agents (with CMR flag), biological agents, noise above action values, vibration, ionising radiation, night work, manual handling, work at height, driving, screen work, and customer-specific factors.
Chemical exposures link to products in the chemical inventory so that the workstation exposure changes when a product is substituted.
painPoints: Free-text exposure descriptions cannot drive surveillance rules or epidemiology.
Exposures recorded at hire and never updated leave workers under-surveilled after a process change.

dependencies.name: Exposure and Risk Profile Register
dependencies.how: Records structured exposures and risk factors per workstation.

dependencies.name: Chemical Product Inventory and Safety Data Sheets
dependencies.how: Links workstation exposures to inventoried products and their hazard classes.

steps.title: Classify each workstation into a surveillance category per country
keyFacts: The physician confirms the category the rules propose: in France 'suivi individuel simple' (VIP) versus 'suivi individuel renforcé' (SIR) with an examen médical d'aptitude; in Belgium periodic health assessment for safety functions, positions with defined risk and increased vigilance; in Luxembourg the 'postes à risques' list; in the Netherlands a PAGO/PMO offer tied to the RI&E.
The physician's override and reasoning are recorded, because the SIR list is the employer's responsibility on the physician's advice and must be presented to the CSE or CPPT.
painPoints: Employers under-declare SIR posts to save medical time and are caught at the next inspection.
Classification decisions taken in a meeting and not written down cannot be reproduced when the physician changes.

dependencies.name: Surveillance Rules and Periodicity Engine
dependencies.how: Proposes the surveillance category from exposures and country rules.

dependencies.name: Country Regulation Content
dependencies.how: Supplies the legal categories and their criteria per country.

dependencies.name: Exposure and Risk Profile Register
dependencies.how: Stores the confirmed category and the physician's justification.

steps.title: Review the profile with the site manager
keyFacts: The site manager confirms that the recorded activities and exposures match the floor, adds tasks the adviser did not see (weekend cleaning with solvents, occasional confined-space entry) and learns what visits the profile will trigger for the team.
The review is a recorded step so that the profile carries a validation date and owner.
painPoints: Profiles written from the office miss the informal tasks that cause most exposures.
Managers learn about SIR obligations only when workers are pulled off the line for visits.

dependencies.name: Exposure and Risk Profile Register
dependencies.how: Records the manager's review and validation date.

dependencies.name: Manager Portal
dependencies.how: Presents the workstation profile to the manager without medical content.

steps.title: Publish the profile and recalculate surveillance for assigned workers
keyFacts: Publishing versions the profile, applies it to every worker assigned to the workstation and recalculates their surveillance; the previous version stays attached to past assignments for exposure history.
The list of workers whose next visit moved is sent to the service coordinator for capacity planning.
painPoints: Unversioned profiles make it impossible to prove what exposure a worker had in a given year.
Profile changes that silently change hundreds of due dates overload the medical agenda if nobody is warned.

dependencies.name: Exposure and Risk Profile Register
dependencies.how: Versions and publishes the workstation profile.

dependencies.name: Surveillance Rules and Periodicity Engine
dependencies.how: Recalculates due visits for assigned workers.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail and Data Retention
dependencies.how: Keeps every profile version with author and date.

streams.name: Plan and schedule medical surveillance
streams.description: Turn surveillance rules and periodicity per country and per profile into a plan the service can deliver: the list of visits due per month and site (visite d'information et de prévention, examen médical d'aptitude under suivi individuel renforcé, Belgian periodic health assessment, visites de reprise and pré-reprise, mid-career visits), a capacity plan per physician and nurse, convocations sent by e-mail or Cegedim SMS with self-service slot choice, reminders that cut no-shows, and a live view of periodicity compliance per site. The service manager steers scarce medical time toward the visits that are legally due first.
outcomes: Periodic surveillance compliance stays above target with the physicians and nurses the service actually has
Convocations go out automatically with the right visit type, duration and examiner, and workers choose or reschedule slots themselves
No-shows drop because reminders reach workers by SMS and e-mail and managers see who is released for a visit
Overdue and at-risk visits are visible per site months in advance, not after the annual report

flows.title: Build the Monthly Surveillance Plan and Send Convocations
flows.description: The service coordinator generates the visits due for the coming period from the periodicity engine, balances them against physician and nurse capacity per site, batches convocations with slot choice, sends reminders and follows confirmations and no-shows.
flows.trigger: The monthly planning cycle opens, or a batch of new hires and transfers adds due visits.
flows.successSignal: Every visit due in the period has a slot, an examiner and a convocation delivered; capacity is not exceeded on any consultation day; confirmations and reschedules are tracked and no-shows are re-convened.

steps.title: Generate the list of visits due for the period
keyFacts: The periodicity engine lists every visit due per worker with its legal basis: a VIP within three months of hire and at most every five years, an examen d'aptitude before assignment to a SIR post and at most every four years with an intermediate nurse visit at two years, night workers every three years, a Belgian periodic health assessment yearly or per the Codex frequency for the risk, a Luxembourg pre-employment examination before starting work.
Overdue visits and visits due within 60 days are ranked first; contract end dates and known absences are shown to avoid convening people who will not be there.
painPoints: Coordinators plan from last year's list and miss transfers into SIR posts.
Visits generated without their legal basis cannot be prioritised when capacity runs short.

dependencies.name: Surveillance Rules and Periodicity Engine
dependencies.how: Derives visit type, due date and legal basis per worker.

dependencies.name: Worker, Contract and Assignment Registry
dependencies.how: Supplies active workers, contract ends and absences.

dependencies.name: Country Regulation Content
dependencies.how: Provides the country intervals and visit types.

steps.title: Balance visits against physician and nurse capacity per site
keyFacts: Capacity is modelled per examiner, site and consultation day with visit durations per type (a nurse VIP, a physician aptitude examination with audiometry, a return-to-work visit); the plan shows utilisation and the backlog that will remain.
Nurse-delegated visits (French VIP by an infirmier en santé au travail under protocol, Belgian nurse follow-up) shift work from the physician where the law allows.
painPoints: Physician time is the scarcest resource in French and Belgian occupational health and is wasted on visits a nurse could run.
Plans that ignore site geography put a physician on the road instead of in consultation.

dependencies.name: Convocation and Appointment Scheduling
dependencies.how: Allocates visits to examiner agendas and consultation days.

dependencies.name: Configuration Engine
dependencies.how: Holds per-customer visit types, durations and nurse delegation settings.

steps.title: Batch and send convocations with slot choice
keyFacts: Convocations are generated per site and visit type in the worker's language (FR/NL/EN), sent by e-mail or by Cegedim SMS for workers without a corporate mailbox, and offer either a fixed slot or a choice of slots in the employee portal.
The manager receives a release notice listing team members to free for their visit, without the reason or medical content.
painPoints: Paper convocations handed out by supervisors are lost, and blue-collar workers with no e-mail are never reached.
Managers who are not told about visits refuse to release workers from the line.

dependencies.how: Creates convocations and slot offers per worker.

dependencies.name: Reminders, SMS and E-mail Notifications
dependencies.how: Sends convocations through e-mail and the Cegedim SMS gateway.

dependencies.name: Employee Portal
dependencies.how: Lets the worker pick or confirm a slot.

dependencies.name: Manager Portal
dependencies.how: Shows the manager which team members have a visit.

steps.title: Send reminders and track confirmations
keyFacts: Reminders go out a set number of days before and the morning of the visit; confirmations, reschedules and cancellations update the agenda in real time.
Delivery status per channel is visible, so an undelivered SMS triggers an e-mail or a call.
painPoints: Services without automated reminders lose a large share of consultation slots to no-shows.
Reminders sent manually stop when the medical secretary is on leave.

dependencies.name: Reminders, SMS and E-mail Notifications
dependencies.how: Sends multi-channel reminders and records delivery.

dependencies.name: Convocation and Appointment Scheduling
dependencies.how: Updates slot status on confirmation, reschedule or cancellation.

steps.title: Handle no-shows and re-convene
keyFacts: A no-show is recorded with a reason where known and the worker is re-convened automatically; repeated no-shows are escalated to the manager and HR, because attending is a legal obligation for the worker and the employer.
The freed slot is offered to a worker on the waiting list on the same site.
painPoints: No-shows quietly become overdue visits that surface only in the annual report.
Escalations by phone leave no trace when HR later needs to prove the employer's diligence.

dependencies.how: Notifies the manager and HR of repeated no-shows.

steps.title: Monitor periodicity compliance per site
keyFacts: The dashboard shows per site and category the share of workers within periodicity, the overdue count and the projected coverage at the end of the quarter if the plan holds.
The coordinator uses it to negotiate extra physician days or a nurse hire before compliance slips.
painPoints: Compliance known only once a year cannot be steered.
Site managers are surprised by an inspection finding of overdue aptitude examinations on their line.

flows.title: Schedule Event-driven Visits (Return to Work, Pre-return, Request by Worker or Employer)
flows.description: HR, the worker or the employer triggers a non-periodic visit — return to work after a long absence, a pre-return visit, a visit at the worker's request, an unplanned visit after an accident — and the service schedules it within the legal delay.
flows.trigger: HR records the end of an absence of 30 days or more (France) or four weeks (Belgium), a worker asks for a visit, or the employer or physician requests one.
flows.successSignal: The visit is scheduled within the legal delay (for a French visite de reprise within eight days of the return), the worker and manager are informed, and the outcome feeds the fitness status and return-to-work coordination.

steps.title: Detect the triggering event from HR data or a request
keyFacts: Absence data from the HRIS flags returns after a work accident, an occupational disease, a maternity leave or an illness above the threshold (in France since the 2022 reform: 30 days after a work accident, 60 days after a non-occupational illness or accident, any duration after an occupational disease or maternity leave; four weeks in Belgium); HR can also raise a request manually.
Workers request a visit from the employee portal at any time without stating a reason, as French and Belgian law entitle them to.
painPoints: HR learns of a return only when the worker reappears, too late for the visit within eight days.
Requests made verbally to the nurse are forgotten in a busy consultation week.

dependencies.name: Worker, Contract and Assignment Registry
dependencies.how: Surfaces absence starts and ends from HR data.

dependencies.name: Surveillance Rules and Periodicity Engine
dependencies.how: Derives the required visit type and legal delay from the event.

dependencies.name: Employee Portal
dependencies.how: Captures a visit request by the worker.

steps.title: Propose a pre-return visit during the absence
keyFacts: During a long absence the physician can offer a visite de pré-reprise (France) or pre-return consultation (Belgium) to prepare adaptations, at the request of the worker, the treating physician or the sickness insurance physician; in the Netherlands the bedrijfsarts's problem analysis by week six under the Wet verbetering poortwachter plays the equivalent role.
The offer is sent through the portal or by SMS and the worker accepts without the employer seeing medical reasons.
painPoints: Adaptations discussed only on the return day delay the actual return by weeks.
Pre-return contacts by the employer risk breaching the worker's privacy; the medical service is the right channel.

dependencies.name: Convocation and Appointment Scheduling
dependencies.how: Schedules the optional pre-return visit.

dependencies.name: Reminders, SMS and E-mail Notifications
dependencies.how: Sends the offer by e-mail or SMS.

dependencies.name: Medical Confidentiality and Access Segregation
dependencies.how: Keeps the pre-return visit and reasons out of the employer's view.

steps.title: Schedule the visit within the legal delay
keyFacts: The nurse books the visit on the first slot inside the legal delay with the right examiner (a return-to-work visit is a physician visit) and duration, and the platform flags visits that will breach the delay so the coordinator can free time.
The employee and manager are notified; the manager sees only the date and that the worker must be released.
painPoints: Return visits booked in the next free slot three weeks later put the employer in breach and leave the worker without a fitness decision.
Managers who plan the return without the visit date assign the worker to the old post prematurely.

dependencies.name: Convocation and Appointment Scheduling
dependencies.how: Books the visit within the legal delay and flags breaches.

dependencies.name: Reminders, SMS and E-mail Notifications
dependencies.how: Notifies worker and manager.

dependencies.name: Manager Portal
dependencies.how: Shows the return visit date without medical content.

steps.title: Coordinate restrictions and adaptations with HR after the visit
keyFacts: Once the physician issues the fitness opinion, HR sees the restrictions and proposed adaptations (adapted hours, no night work, no lifting above a weight, part-time therapeutic return) and records what the employer put in place and when.
In France an inaptitude opinion opens the employer's one-month reclassification search; the platform tracks the deadline and the exchanges with the physician.
painPoints: Restrictions communicated by paper certificate reach the manager days later and are applied inconsistently.
Reclassification deadlines missed by HR expose the employer to reinstated salary payments and litigation.

dependencies.name: Consultation Workspace and Fitness Opinions
dependencies.how: Provides the opinion, restrictions and adaptations.

dependencies.name: Worker, Contract and Assignment Registry
dependencies.how: Records applied adaptations against the assignment.

dependencies.name: Reminders, SMS and E-mail Notifications
dependencies.how: Reminds HR of reclassification and follow-up deadlines.

steps.title: Plan the follow-up visit and close the event
keyFacts: If the physician asked for a follow-up (temporary restrictions, part-time return), it is scheduled at once and the event is closed when the worker is back on an assignment consistent with the opinion.
The whole event chain is kept as one record for the annual report and for a later dispute.
painPoints: Follow-ups agreed verbally are never booked and temporary restrictions become permanent by default.
Events closed in HR and open in the medical service produce contradictory reports.

dependencies.name: Convocation and Appointment Scheduling
dependencies.how: Schedules the follow-up visit.

dependencies.name: Surveillance Rules and Periodicity Engine
dependencies.how: Closes the event when the follow-up is done and periodicity resumes.

streams.name: Conduct examinations and teleconsultations
streams.description: Run a complete examination from convocation to signed opinion: the worker completes the pre-visit questionnaire privately in the portal, the nurse runs intake and screenings with connected audiometry, spirometry and vision devices whose readings land directly in the record, the physician works in a consultation workspace that shows the file, exposures and history, issues the fitness-for-work opinion with restrictions and accommodations, signs it electronically through Goodflag, and can run the whole conversation as a secure Vonage teleconsultation where the law and the visit type allow. Nurse visits and vaccination or health campaigns run on the same workspace at scale.
outcomes: Every examination ends with a documented, signed fitness opinion on the day of the visit, with restrictions the employer can apply
Screening results from connected devices are captured without retyping, cutting data capture errors and consultation documentation time
Pre-visit questionnaires completed in advance shorten the intake and let the physician focus on the clinical conversation
Teleconsultation extends physician reach to remote sites and follow-ups without moving medical data outside the HDS environment
Vaccination and health campaigns reach the whole eligible population with individual records in the file

flows.title: Run a Consultation Day from Intake to Signed Fitness Opinion
flows.description: On a consultation day the nurse prepares the agenda, checks questionnaires, runs screenings with connected devices, the physician conducts the examination, issues and signs the fitness opinion, and the certificates reach the worker and the employer in their respective versions.
flows.trigger: The consultation day opens with the scheduled visits (periodic, aptitude, return-to-work, on request) on the site or in the service's premises.
flows.successSignal: Every worker seen has a completed consultation record, device measurements attached, a signed fitness opinion in the file and the employer-facing certificate delivered without medical content; no visit remains 'open' at the end of the day.

steps.title: Prepare the day's agenda and check pre-visit questionnaires
keyFacts: The nurse sees the day's visits with type, examiner and duration, and which workers have completed the pre-visit questionnaire (medical history, symptoms, work situation, questionnaires adapted to the exposure such as a night-work sleep questionnaire or a respiratory questionnaire for dust exposure).
Workers who did not complete it in the portal are given a tablet on arrival; the questionnaire is under medical secrecy and never visible to HR.
painPoints: Paper questionnaires filled in the waiting room are illegible and retyped after the visit.
Nurses discover missing files and wrong visit types only when the worker is already in the room.

dependencies.name: Convocation and Appointment Scheduling
dependencies.how: Lists the day's visits with type and examiner.

dependencies.name: Questionnaires and Pre-visit Intake
dependencies.how: Shows completion and opens the questionnaire for on-site completion.

dependencies.name: Employee Portal
dependencies.how: Lets the worker complete the questionnaire in advance.

steps.title: Run intake and screenings with connected devices
keyFacts: The nurse records height, weight, blood pressure and vision, runs audiometry for noise-exposed posts and spirometry for dust or chemical exposures; Eolys, FIM, Essilor, JLM Medical and Siemens devices push readings straight into the consultation record with device, date and calibration.
Results are compared with the worker's previous measurements so that a hearing threshold shift or a drop in FEV1 is flagged for the physician before the examination.
painPoints: Retyping audiograms from device printouts is the main source of screening data errors.
Trend comparison by hand across paper files is impossible during a busy day.

dependencies.name: Medical Device Measurement Capture
dependencies.how: Receives measurements from connected devices into the record.

dependencies.name: Ecosystem Integrations
dependencies.how: Bridges device middleware to the platform.

dependencies.name: Consultation Workspace and Fitness Opinions
dependencies.how: Shows results against previous values and flags shifts.

steps.title: Conduct the examination in the consultation workspace
keyFacts: The physician sees in one screen the worker's assignment and exposures, the surveillance category and legal basis of the visit, the questionnaire, screenings, previous opinions and the medical file, and documents the examination with structured findings and free text.

The workspace enforces the visit's legal content: a French examen d'aptitude under SIR requires the aptitude decision; a Belgian periodic assessment requires the 'formulaire d'évaluation de la santé'.
painPoints: Physicians spend more time navigating files than talking to the worker.
Examinations documented in a generic EHR miss the occupational context that the aptitude decision depends on.

dependencies.name: Consultation Workspace and Fitness Opinions
dependencies.how: Captures the examination and its structured findings.

dependencies.name: Occupational Medical File
dependencies.how: Presents history, previous opinions and documents.

dependencies.name: Exposure and Risk Profile Register
dependencies.how: Shows the workstation's exposures and surveillance category.

steps.title: Issue the fitness opinion with restrictions and accommodations
keyFacts: The physician selects the conclusion (fit, fit with restrictions or adaptations, temporarily unfit, unfit, or in France an 'attestation de suivi' after a VIP) and records restrictions in structured terms the employer can apply: no night work, no work at height, maximum load, adapted workstation, part-time.

streams.name: Keep the occupational medical file
streams.description: Keep one complete and confidential occupational medical file per worker (the French DMST under law 2021-1018 and decree 2022-1434, the Belgian health file of the Codex, the Luxembourg and Dutch equivalents): every consultation, measurement, questionnaire, document, exposure and opinion in one place, under medical secrecy with access segregated between physician, nurse, medical secretary, HR and manager; retention for the legal period after the end of exposure; transfer of the file when the worker changes service or employer; and interoperability with national health records such as the French Dossier Médical Partagé where the worker consents.
outcomes: The medical file is complete and follows the worker across sites, services and employers, so the physician always examines with the full history
Medical secrecy is enforced by design: HR and managers never see medical content, and every access is logged
Files are retained for the legal period (40 years after the last visit for a French DMST) and destroyed or archived on schedule
Transfers between services and interoperability with national records are handled with consent and traceability

flows.title: Maintain the File under Medical Secrecy

flows.trigger: Any contact with the worker (visit, screening, campaign, document received) or a worker's request for access to their own file.
flows.successSignal: The file reflects every contact, external documents are classified and attached, only authorised roles have seen medical content, and the worker's access request was answered within the legal delay.

steps.title: Create or retrieve the worker's file
keyFacts: A file is created at the first contact from the worker registry, or retrieved from a previous service when the worker arrives with a transfer; identity is matched on HR identifiers and civil status to avoid duplicates.
Kitry customers hold more than 4 million employee records, many with decades of history migrated from previous systems.
painPoints: Duplicate files created for a returning worker split the exposure history.
Files kept per site mean a worker transferred between plants is examined without history.

Measurements stored as PDFs cannot be trended across years.

rootGroups.name: Workplace Safety and Event Streams
rootGroups.description: From workstations and products to a living risk assessment, closed corrective actions and correctly declared events: the journeys that assess and control risks, report and resolve hazardous situations, track chemical products and exposures, and declare and analyse accidents and occupational diseases.

streams.name: Assess and control workplace risks
streams.description: Maintain a living risk assessment per workstation, unit and site — the French DUERP (document unique d'évaluation des risques professionnels), the Belgian global prevention plan and annual action plan built on the dynamic risk management system, the Luxembourg risk inventory and the Dutch RI&E with its plan van aanpak — with prevention measures, residual risk, the annual update and consultation of the CSE or CPPT, and the evidence an ISO 45001 management system needs. The prevention adviser assesses with site managers, the physician contributes the health view, and the action plan flows into follow-up.
outcomes: The risk assessment is current for every workstation and updated when the workplace changes, not just once a year before the inspection
Prevention measures and residual risks are linked to the exposures the medical service surveils, so health and safety reason from the same facts
The annual update, the CSE/CPPT consultation and the action plan (PAPRIPACT, annual action plan) are produced from the assessment, not rewritten
ISO 45001 clauses on hazard identification, legal requirements and planning are evidenced from the same data

flows.title: Assess a Site and Publish the Prevention Plan
flows.description: The prevention adviser assesses each workstation of a site with the site manager, rates hazards, records existing and planned measures, involves the physician on health risks, consults the CSE or CPPT and publishes the assessment and its action plan.
flows.trigger: A site is added, the annual update is due, a significant change in working conditions occurs, or an accident or occupational disease reveals a new risk.
flows.successSignal: Every workstation of the site has rated hazards, measures and residual risk; the assessment is versioned and dated, the CSE/CPPT consultation is recorded, and the action plan items are assigned with deadlines.

steps.title: Walk the workstations with the site manager
keyFacts: The adviser assesses on the floor with the manager, using the workstation list shared with the medical service, and records hazards per activity: machinery, manual handling, chemicals, noise, falls, vehicles, psychosocial risks, lone work.
Observations, photos and worker interviews are captured on a tablet and attached to the workstation.
painPoints: Assessments done from the office reproduce last year's text.
Hazards recorded per department instead of per workstation cannot be linked to the workers exposed.

steps.title: Rate risks and record existing prevention measures
keyFacts: Each hazard is rated on the customer's method (severity x probability x exposure, or the Kinney method common in Belgium) with the existing collective and individual measures, and the residual risk; the rating method is configured per customer and consistent across sites.
Chemical hazards pull the CLP classification from the inventory; physical exposures pull measurements (noise, vibration) where they exist.
painPoints: Different sites using different rating scales make group-level prioritisation meaningless.
Measures that exist only on paper (unused extraction, expired PPE) are counted as controls.

keyFacts: The physician reviews the health-related hazards, links them to the workstation's exposure profile and surveillance category, and adds the medical view (collective indicators such as hearing shifts on a line) without disclosing individual data.
In Belgium the physician-prevention adviser's contribution is a required part of the global prevention plan; in France the physician's 'fiche d'entreprise' feeds the DUERP.
painPoints: Risk assessments written without the physician miss the exposures that cause occupational diseases.
Physicians asked for input by e-mail have no view of the assessment context.

keyFacts: For risks above the acceptance threshold, the adviser plans measures with owner, cost, deadline and expected residual risk; they form the French PAPRIPACT or the Belgian annual action plan derived from the global prevention plan.
Measures are created as actions in the action plan so that progress is followed in the same place as inspection and hazardous situation actions.

Measures without owners and budgets are re-planned every year.

streams.name: Report and resolve hazardous situations
streams.description: Take a hazardous situation reported from the floor, a near miss, an inspection observation or an audit non-conformity to a corrective action that is assigned, followed and closed with evidence. Employees and managers report from the portal or a phone with photo and location; the prevention adviser qualifies and assigns; the site manager fixes and proves it; the HSE manager watches closure rates and repeat situations. outcomes: Hazardous situations reach the prevention adviser within minutes with photo and location, and the reporter sees what happened to the report
Corrective actions are owned, dated and closed with evidence, with closure rates visible per site
Inspections and safety walks run on checklists and turn findings into actions without re-entry
Repeat situations and slow closures are visible so that prevention resources go where they matter

streams.name: Track chemical products and exposures

streams.name: Declare and analyse accidents and occupational diseases

rootGroups.name: Experience and Insight Streams
rootGroups.description: From role-based portals and cross-module data to self-service for every employee and manager and steerable performance for the service and HSE managers: the journeys that serve employees and managers through portals and monitor health and safety performance.

streams.name: Serve employees and managers through portals
streams.description: Give every employee and every manager a role-based portal on the same platform: employees book and reschedule visits, complete questionnaires privately, download their certificates and vaccination record, join a teleconsultation and report a safety concern, in French, Dutch or English, with SSO or an SMS code; managers see the fitness clearance and restrictions of their team without medical content, release workers for visits, own corrective actions and record accidents. More than half of the workers at Kitry's French, Belgian and Luxembourg customers use self-service, which relieves the medical service of the administrative load and gives managers a lawful view of team fitness.
outcomes: Most workers manage their own visits and documents, cutting administrative work in the medical service
Managers know who on their team is cleared, restricted or overdue for a visit, without ever seeing a diagnosis
Questionnaires are completed before the visit under medical secrecy, shortening consultation time
Safety concerns and accidents are reported from the floor within minutes and followed to closure

flows.title: Manage My Visits and Documents as an Employee
flows.description: An employee receives a convocation, signs in to the portal, chooses or reschedules a slot, completes the questionnaire, attends (in person or by video), acknowledges the certificate and later downloads documents and reports a concern.
flows.trigger: The employee receives a convocation by e-mail or SMS, or wants to see their documents or report a safety concern.
flows.successSignal: The employee has booked a slot, completed the questionnaire before the visit, received and acknowledged the certificate in the portal, and can find their documents; no HR or manager saw questionnaire or medical content.

steps.title: Sign in with corporate SSO or an SMS code
keyFacts: Office staff sign in with corporate SSO; plant, depot and field workers without a mailbox receive a one-time code by Cegedim SMS on their personal phone; consent to the use of the personal number is recorded.
The portal is available in FR/NL/EN on any device without an app store install.
painPoints: Portals that need a corporate account exclude the workers with the highest exposures.
Shared kiosk logins breach confidentiality.

The manager sees the resulting release date in the manager portal.
painPoints: Reschedules by phone to the medical secretary consume hours a week.
Slots chosen after the legal due date silently create non-compliance.

Questionnaires filled in the waiting room are rushed.

A fallback to a physical visit is offered when the connection fails.
painPoints: Video links by e-mail are lost or opened on the wrong day.
Workers without a quiet room cannot do a confidential video visit.

Documents remain available after the employee leaves the company for the period the customer configures.

Acknowledgement by signature on paper delays the file.

Reports go to the prevention adviser, not to the line manager alone.

flows.title: Steer My Team's Fitness, Restrictions and Actions as a Manager

flows.successSignal: The manager has applied every current restriction, released workers for their visits, recorded events promptly and closed assigned actions, and has never seen medical content.

Contractors and temporary workers on the site can be included where the customer manages them.

Team lists in HR do not show restrictions.

steps.title: Apply restrictions and record adaptations

streams.name: Monitor health and safety performance
streams.description: Turn cross-module data into steering: dashboards and KPIs for the service manager, the HSE manager and the employer (surveillance coverage, medical capacity utilisation, accident rates, action closure, chemical inventory completeness), the regulatory and annual reports each country expects (the French annual activity report of the occupational physician and the SPST, the Belgian annual report of the internal prevention service and the global prevention plan follow-up, the Dutch RI&E follow-up, ISO 45001 management review inputs), and collective health monitoring that links exposures to anonymised health indicators to advise the employer on prevention.
outcomes: Service and HSE managers steer from live indicators instead of learning the position from the annual report
Annual and regulatory reports are produced from the platform in a fraction of the preparation time, with consistent figures
Collective health monitoring turns individual findings into prevention advice without breaching individual secrecy
The employer, the CSE/CPPT and the authorities receive consistent, traceable figures

flows.title: Produce the Annual Activity and Prevention Reports
flows.description: The service manager and the HSE manager assemble the annual reports from platform data, review them with the physician, present them to the works council and the employer and file them where required.

Multi-country groups produce one report per country from one dataset.
painPoints: Report templates copied from last year miss new mandatory sections.
Group reports built from site spreadsheets do not reconcile.

Figures are traceable to the underlying records for the physician's review, within secrecy.

Figures that cannot be traced are contested by the employer.

Prevention plan progress is described qualitatively because nobody tracked it.

Physicians validate reports whose figures they cannot check.

Worker representatives get read access to the report.

Committee opinions are not recorded with the report.

flows.successSignal: The signal is confirmed or dismissed with data, the employer receives documented prevention advice, actions are created and the indicators show the effect over time.

Each persona has a default dashboard: service manager, HSE manager, physician, HR, employer.
painPoints: Managers run on last quarter's figures.
One dashboard for everyone shows too much to some and too little to others.

dependencies.name: Dashboards and KPIs

dependencies.name: Identity, SSO, Roles and Consent

steps.title: Detect a collective health signal on a population

Only the physician sees the aggregated medical indicators; the employer sees what the physician releases.
painPoints: Individual findings are never combined and clusters go unnoticed for years.
Aggregations on small groups identify individuals.

dependencies.name: Collective Health Monitoring
dependencies.how: Aggregates findings and flags deviations.

dependencies.name: Medical Confidentiality and Access Segregation
dependencies.how: Suppresses identifiable aggregations.

dependencies.name: Exposure and Risk Profile Register

steps.title: Investigate the signal with the prevention adviser

The investigation is documented as a case with its data views.
painPoints: Signals discussed by e-mail without the safety data.
Investigations not documented are redone at the next signal.

streams.name: Deploy, migrate and train a customer
streams.description: Take a new organisation from contract to go-live and beyond on Kitry's four-phase method — functional assessment, configuration, project management and training — with data migration of decades of medical files, exposure histories and accident records from legacy systems, change management for physicians, nurses, HSE, HR, managers and employees, and after go-live the regulatory and product release train, support and a dedicated account manager. Kitry's consultants run this on the same platform, on shared or dedicated HDS SaaS, for customers such as SNCF, Ville de Paris, Umicore or BNP.
outcomes: Customers go live on schedule with their data migrated, their configuration validated by the physician and HSE, and their users trained
Migration defects are found and fixed before go-live, so no medical file or exposure history is lost
Regulatory and product releases reach every customer without disruption and with the right functional communication
Support requests are resolved within target and the account manager grows the modules and self-service adoption

flows.title: Run the Four-phase Implementation to Go-live

The service manager, the physician, the HSE manager and HR each validate their part of the assessment.
painPoints: Requirements gathered from IT alone miss the physician's daily practice.
Assessments without recorded decisions are re-litigated during configuration.

Country regulation content (FR/BE/LU/NL) is activated per legal entity.

Changes that affect a customer's configuration are flagged for the account manager.

Releases without functional release notes surprise physicians mid-consultation.

Recurring requests feed configuration improvements and training.
painPoints: Support that needs medical data access without control breaches secrecy.
Recurring questions answered one by one instead of fixed.

streams.name: Integrate with HR, devices and the ecosystem
streams.description: Connect the platform to the systems around it so that data flows without re-entry and the platform stays inside its certified boundary: HRIS synchronisation, SSO with the customer's identity provider, Goodflag electronic signature, Vonage teleconsultation, Cegedim SMS, connected measurement devices from Eolys, FIM, Essilor, JLM Medical and Siemens, national reporting connectors for accident and disease declarations, and the shared or dedicated HDS/ISO 27001 hosting environments in the EEA that every integration must respect.
outcomes: HR changes, signatures, video sessions, SMS and device readings flow into the platform without re-entry and without medical data leaving the HDS boundary
New customers connect their HRIS and identity provider with standard connectors rather than projects
Device and partner integrations are monitored so that a failed connector is seen before a consultation day is disrupted
National reporting connectors keep declarations working when portals and forms change

flows.title: Connect a Customer's HRIS and Identity Provider
flows.description: The Kitry consultant and the HR administrator set up the HRIS feed and SSO for a new customer, map fields and roles, test on a sample and the full population, and put the connection under monitoring.
flows.primaryActor: Kitry Implementation and Customer Success Consultant
flows.trigger: A new customer, a change of HRIS or identity provider, or a change in the HR data model.
flows.successSignal: The HRIS feed runs on schedule with reconciled counts, SSO signs users in with the right roles, and both connections are monitored with alerts.

steps.title: Agree the data contract with HR and IT
steps.actor: Kitry Implementation and Customer Success Consultant
keyFacts: The consultant and HR agree the fields (identifiers, civil status, contract, assignment, site, absences), the frequency, the transport (SFTP file, API) and the handling of sensitive fields; the contract is recorded as the connector configuration.
Data protection roles (controller, processor) and the processing record are confirmed with the customer's DPO.
painPoints: Feeds built without a contract break at the first HR system change.
HR exporting more than needed creates a data protection issue.

dependencies.name: HRIS Synchronisation and Import
dependencies.how: Records fields, frequency and transport.

dependencies.name: Ecosystem Integrations
dependencies.how: Configures the SFTP or API transport.

steps.title: Map fields and organisational structures
keyFacts: HR codes are mapped to platform values (contract types, units to sites and workstations, absence types to surveillance triggers); the mapping is configuration, versioned and testable.
Unmapped values are routed to an exception list rather than dropped.
painPoints: Hard-coded mappings that only the integrator understands.
Unmapped absence types that never trigger the return visit.

dependencies.name: HRIS Synchronisation and Import
dependencies.how: Maintains versioned mappings and exception routing.

dependencies.name: Configuration Engine
dependencies.how: Stores mapping rules as configuration.

steps.title: Configure SSO and role mapping
steps.actor: Kitry Implementation and Customer Success Consultant
keyFacts: SAML or OpenID Connect is configured with the customer's identity provider; directory groups are mapped to platform roles (physician, nurse, HSE, HR, manager, employee) and to perimeters (sites, entities); provisioning and deprovisioning follow the directory.
Medical roles require a second assignment by the service manager, so a directory error cannot grant medical access.
painPoints: Role mapping errors that give HR access to medical content.
Leavers keeping access because deprovisioning is manual.

dependencies.name: Identity, SSO, Roles and Consent
dependencies.how: Configures the identity provider and role mapping.

dependencies.name: Medical Confidentiality and Access Segregation

steps.title: Test on a sample and on the full population
steps.actor: Kitry Implementation and Customer Success Consultant
keyFacts: The feed is run in a validation tenant on a sample and then the full population; counts per entity and site are reconciled with HR, exceptions reviewed, and SSO tested per role.
The test results are signed off by HR and the service manager.
painPoints: Full-population issues (duplicates, encoding, historical contracts) appear only in production.
Sign-off by IT alone misses functional errors.

dependencies.name: HRIS Synchronisation and Import
dependencies.how: Runs and reconciles test loads.

dependencies.name: Implementation, Migration and Training Workspace
dependencies.how: Records test results and sign-off.

steps.title: Put the connections under monitoring
steps.actor: Kitry Implementation and Customer Success Consultant
keyFacts: The feed and SSO are monitored for missed runs, reject rates and authentication failures; alerts go to the customer's HR administrator and to Kitry support; the audit trail keeps every batch.
Monitoring is part of the HDS/ISO 27001 operations evidence.
painPoints: Feeds that silently stop for weeks are discovered when a hire has no visit.
Authentication failures blamed on the platform when the directory changed.

dependencies.name: Ecosystem Integrations
dependencies.how: Monitors runs and raises alerts.

dependencies.name: Audit Trail and Data Retention
dependencies.how: Keeps batch history.

flows.title: Operate Partner, Device and National Reporting Integrations
flows.description: The consultant and the nurse connect measurement devices, the Kitry integrations team operates the Goodflag, Vonage, Cegedim and national reporting connectors inside the HDS boundary and handles partner changes without disrupting consultation days.
flows.primaryActor: Kitry Implementation and Customer Success Consultant
flows.trigger: A site installs devices, a partner changes its API or a national portal changes its form, or a connector fails.
flows.successSignal: Devices push readings into consultations, signatures, video sessions and SMS work through the partners, national submissions succeed, and every integration respects the HDS boundary and is monitored.

steps.title: Install and pair measurement devices on a site
keyFacts: Audiometers, spirometers, vision testers and other devices from Eolys, FIM, Essilor, JLM Medical and Siemens are paired with the consultation workstation through the device connector; a test reading is captured and calibration data is recorded.
Devices without a supported driver are captured through a manual entry with the same structure.
painPoints: Device software that writes to a local folder nobody backs up.
Uncalibrated devices produce results the physician cannot trust.

Partner contracts and data processing agreements are kept per customer.
painPoints: A partner API change breaking signatures on a consultation day.
SMS credits exhausted without warning before a convocation batch.

keyFacts: Connectors and forms for net-entreprises/Ameli, Belgian insurers and Fedris, the Luxembourg AAA and the Dutch Arbeidsinspectie are updated when portals or forms change; the regulatory content team flags the change and the integrations team ships it before the mandatory date.
Submission failures are reported to HR with the reason and a manual fallback.
painPoints: Declarations rejected by a portal after a silent form change.
HR without a fallback misses the 48-hour deadline.

steps.title: Enforce the HDS boundary for every integration
steps.actor: Kitry Implementation and Customer Success Consultant
keyFacts: Every integration is reviewed for what data leaves the platform: signatures carry the document hash and signer identity, video sessions are brokered without recording, SMS carry no medical content, device readings flow inbound only; all endpoints and hosting stay in the EEA.
The review is part of the HDS and ISO 27001 control set and is repeated at each partner change.
painPoints: Convenient integrations that leak medical content into a partner's logs.
Partners hosting outside the EEA discovered at the certification audit.

Incident history feeds the customer's certification evidence and the partner review.

Incidents without customer communication erode trust.
